text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- U.S. subsidiaries of Dutch companies donate a total of a quarter million dollars to American election campaign. (p1)
- Royal Dutch/Shell's Q3 net up 26 pct to Dfl 3.47 bn, boosted by higher oil prices. (p1)
- Paper and packaging maker KNP BT reports sharply lower Q3 net at Dfl 29 million due to losses at paper unit KNP Leykam. (p1)
- Government sets aside ten million guilders for small and medium-sized businesses that want to obtain information about exporting. (p1)
- Entertainment group Endemol's issue 25 times oversubscribed in spite of earlier closing of offering. (p1)
- Dutch credit insurer NCM signs cooperation agreement with Belgian counterpart Belgische Kredietbank. (p3)
- Builder Kondor Wessels is expecting profit growth to continue. (p5)
- ABN Amro bank takes 40 pct stake in South African stock broker Huysamer Stals. (p13)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Traffic minister seeks to break monopoly of public transport company VSN. (p1)
- Mysterious buyer active in obtaining retailer De Boer shares. (p2)
- Britain's food group Perkins Foods takes over wholesaler Disselkoen. (p2)
- Environmental activists start new actions against Shell's activities in Nigeria. (p15)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Current Overseas Development minister Jan Pronk slept through many a ministerial meeting of the Den Uyl cabinet (1973- 76), according to a book. (p1)
- Central bank president Wim Duisenberg gives instruction about the new European currency at a primary school. (p1)
- Amsterdam Stock Exchange Board leaves decision on merger with European Option Exchange until necessary provision for contingencies is clarified. (p27)
- Holland Colours (HCA) books 12 pct higher first half net at Dfl 2.7 million. (p29)
TROUW
- Favourable review by Washington Post of Dutch author Harry Mulisch's book "The Discovery of Heaven". (p1)
- "Green investments", already very popular, are to be made still more appealing fiscally. (p7)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Money printer Joh. Enschede expects considerable job loss due to missing out on orders for European single currency Euro. (p1)
- Justice department fears money laundering with exchanging guilders for the Euro. (p3)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
